open_questions.question: When the Wikipedia master's Units sold values are revised (e.g., Toyota Corolla incrementing past 50M as production continues), should the instance be re-staged?
open_questions.answer: Yes. 8 of 10 rows are active-production nameplates whose cumulative-units-sold increment annually; master may revise Units sold values when manufacturers publish updated cumulative reports. temporal_sensitivity = low because the relative top-10 ordering shifts slowly (the rank-1/rank-2 Corolla/F-Series gap of 7M units is wide enough to be stable; Honda Accord is the tenth and final row of the cited master table at 19.5M, and the instance asserts no cutoff beyond the master's ten rows — the master lists no eleventh row and caveats that cumulative-sales figures have no definitive measurement standard). Re-staging on master revision is straightforward — replace cell values, no schema or universe-identity change needed.

open_questions.question: Why is the Volkswagen Beetle treated as a single nameplate spanning 1938-2003 when there were Type 1 + New Beetle eras?
open_questions.answer: Per Wikipedia master scope. The master's 'Best-selling car nameplates of all time' table lists 'Volkswagen Beetle | 1938–2003 | 21.5 million' as a single row — this is the Volkswagen Type 1. The staged row reproduces that master row verbatim (1938–2003, 21.5M). The Volkswagen New Beetle (1997–2011) is a separate successor model; per the Volkswagen Beetle and New Beetle Wikipedia pages it is NOT part of the Type 1's 21.5M figure, and the master does not aggregate it into this row. The curator neither splits nor merges the nameplate; the row is exactly the master's Type 1 entry.

open_questions.question: Why is Ford HQ normalized to 'United States' instead of the manufacturer page's verbatim 'US'?

open_questions.question: Why is Toyota Hilux at rank 9 not higher? It's a popular global pickup.
open_questions.answer: Per master's verbatim Units sold ranking. Hilux's 21M cumulative units span 1968-present (58 years). Toyota Camry at rank 6 with 22M units across only 1982-present (44 years) reflects higher annual sales-rate; Hilux's slower per-year sales rate is offset partially by its longer production history but not enough to push it above Camry. Master ranks by cumulative Units sold DESC + this is the canonical universe.

open_questions.question: What's the database structure of the implicit_join framing?
open_questions.answer: Per cycle-2-rewritten db_analog: top_10_automobiles CTE = Wikipedia master rows with Manufacturer DETERMINISTICALLY DERIVED from Nameplate column via leading-prefix token rule (`derive_manufacturer_from_nameplate(nameplate)` per cycle-2 audit clarification — master table has 4 columns Nameplate/Production/Units sold/Notes with NO separate Manufacturer column), sorted by units_sold_millions DESC + master_row_position ASC tiebreak LIMIT 10; INNER JOIN with manufacturer_pages table on `normalize_manufacturer_identity(a.manufacturer) = normalize_manufacturer_identity(m.manufacturer_name)` — the normalize_manufacturer_identity() intermediate accommodates Wikipedia-master derived short forms ('Toyota' / 'Ford' / 'Volkswagen' / 'Honda') vs per-manufacturer-page longer corporate forms ('Toyota Motor Corporation' / 'Ford Motor Company' / 'Volkswagen AG' / 'Honda Motor Co.'); final SELECT extracts Model (from Nameplate) + Manufacturer (derived) + Cumulative Units Sold (millions) + Production Years + HQ Country ordered by Cumulative Units Sold DESC + master_row_position ASC tiebreak. The implicit-join is on manufacturer-identity dimension; HQ Country is value-supplemented from per-manufacturer pages (4 unique manufacturer rows joined to 10 model rows, fanned-out). Mirror precedent: cycle-2 PulitzerTonyPlays normalized-identity-join pattern.
